summary: A Slack app works in your own workspace the minute you create it - there is no gate at all for that. Review only enters the picture when you want other workspaces to install it through public distribution.

rationale: Single-workspace apps need no approval, which keeps the common case simple.
Public distribution goes through Slack's app review, and reviewers check that every scope is justified.
The OAuth flow itself is standard and well documented.

timeEstimate.setup: Under an hour to create the app, add redirect URLs and run the OAuth flow against your own workspace.
timeEstimate.approval: For public distribution, plan for a few days to about two weeks of Marketplace review, plus time to fix anything reviewers flag.

basis.text: Slack's app review documentation describes the distribution review; no fixed SLA is published.
Review duration is an estimate - Slack does not guarantee a timeline.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps, choose Create New App, and pick 'from scratch'. The app is live in your workspace immediately.

steps.title: Add scopes and redirect URLs
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions, add only the bot/user scopes you actually call, and register your HTTPS redirect URL.

steps.title: Install and test in your workspace
steps.detail: Use the install URL to walk the OAuth flow yourself. Everything works here without any review.

steps.title: Turn on public distribution and submit
steps.detail: Under Manage Distribution, complete the checklist (install link, redirect URLs, removing hard-coded workspace references) and submit for review.

requirements.item: A Slack account and a workspace where you can create apps
HTTPS redirect URLs, registered on the app's OAuth settings page
A short explanation of what each requested scope is for (asked during review)

gotchas.text: Asking for scopes you don't use is the most common reason reviews bounce back.
Bot tokens and user tokens are different things in Slack - check which one each API method expects.
Socket Mode is handy for development but doesn't replace the OAuth install flow for distribution.

agentCanDo: Read Slack's current auth and app-review docs and refresh this guide
Map your feature list to the smallest scope set
Draft the scope justifications reviewers ask for
developerMustDo: Create the app under their own Slack account and workspace
Complete the distribution checklist and submit for review
